Transform this image into a highly realistic embroidered patch.
Recreate the entire image as if it were professionally machine embroidered, combining dense tatami (fill) stitches and satin (full) stitches for a robust and premium look.

Keep the original composition, proportions, perspective, identity, scale and exact positioning exactly the same.
Do not crop, rotate, zoom, reposition or reframe the subject.
Maintain the exact same alignment and framing as the original image.

Use dense tatami (fill) stitches for larger colored areas.
Use satin (full) stitches for borders, smaller shapes, lettering and key highlights.
Maintain the exact same original colors inside the design.
Follow the natural direction of each shape when placing stitches.
Simulate realistic thread texture with visible fibers and subtle thread shine.
Create depth using stitch direction changes instead of digital gradients.
Add realistic stitch layering where shapes overlap.
Include subtle shadows between stitch rows to enhance dimensional depth.

Keep edges clean and well-defined with stitch boundaries.
Create a thick, structured embroidered border around the entire design using satin stitches.
The border color must be CUSTOM_BORDER_COLOR.
The border color must be uniform and solid.
Do not change the internal design colors.
The border must look dense, slightly raised and professionally stitched.

The patch must be isolated on a pure white background (#FFFFFF).
No shadows on the background.
No gradients.
No textures outside the patch.
No environment.
The white background must be flat, clean and uniform.

Photorealistic embroidery.
Macro photography look.
High thread detail.
Studio lighting focused only on the patch.
No cartoon effect.
No smooth digital painting.
No vector style.
The final result must look like a real embroidered patch photographed in a professional studio, perfectly centered and isolated on a solid white background.

Ultra-clean and hyper-detailed restoration and colorization of an old historical photograph, preserving the original framing, composition, and proportions.

Task: Restore and colorize an old historical photo.

Instructions:
- Remove blur, scratches, stains, discoloration, and digital artifacts while keeping the authentic archival character of the photo.
- Preserve the original framing, composition, and proportions exactly as in the source image.
- Do NOT crop, distort, or alter the perspective.
- Maintain the historical integrity and realism of the photograph.

- Enhance natural textures such as facial details, wrinkles, hair strands, clothing fabric, and background surfaces with photoreal clarity.
- Apply realistic and natural colorization while respecting historical accuracy.
- Keep the faces exactly the same as in the provided image (no modification of identity or features).
- Do NOT stylize, cartoonize, or reinterpret the image.
- Final result must look like a perfectly restored and naturally colorized real photograph.
